MODEL_FEEDBACK_JSON:
{
  "positive_alignment_reasons": [
    "Josh Groban feels like a natural next choice because I want expressive singing with orchestral arrangements, consistent with my interest in Stages, Il Divo, and The Tenors.",
    "To Be Loved appeals through polished vocal standards, while Come Away with Me offers the gentle singing and relaxed mood that fit my current interest in soothing music."
  ],
  "negative_misalignment_reasons": [
    "Clear As Day, Blown Away, and Carnival Ride connect to my past country listening, but that connection is not enough when I want calmer vocal performances today.",
    "O Brother, Where Art Thou? shares a soundtrack connection with Downton Abbey, but its roots-oriented sound does not offer the same orchestral appeal. Whitney Houston and Huey Lewis also feel less suited to the gentle mood I want.",
    "Home for Christmas connects to an earlier Christmas album, but enjoying seasonal music before does not mean I want it now."
  ],
  "overgeneralized_signals": [
    "My country purchases seem to have been treated as a broad invitation to recommend more country, without enough attention to the sound I currently want.",
    "Past soundtrack and Christmas listening seem to have been carried forward too broadly; those connections alone do not make an album appealing today."
  ],
  "missing_or_underweighted_signals": [
    "My latest interest in relaxing classical music makes a soothing mood especially relevant to what I would choose now.",
    "The connection across my vocal albums is expressive, polished singing with rich arrangements; that matters more to me than simply sharing a broad music label or being a soundtrack."
  ],
  "summary_diagnosis": "The recommendations partly understood my taste for polished vocals, but gave too much weight to older country and seasonal listening and too little to my current preference for soothing arrangements."
}
